definition: The AI -- or a fuzzing script or harness the AI wrote -- discovered or reported the defect: a Reported-by credit naming an AI tool or a vendor's AI security research team ('OpenAI Codex Security', 'in collaboration with Claude and Anthropic Research'), or prose such as 'Claude Code found this problem', 'I had Opus look for bugs in recent commits', 'found using a fuzz script I asked Claude Code to write'.

The human already had the problem or a patch in hand and used the AI to understand, diagnose, review, cross-check, re-verify or explain it: 'I asked Claude to confirm this', 'AI tells me this requires an xid', 'I asked some LLMs about this', 'Gemini told me how HMAC_Init_ex works', 'I fed your version into Chat-GPT', an Analyzed-by credit, an AI review of a patch, an AI-written analysis of the code.

The AI wrote or drafted something that is part of the submission: the patch or a prototype of it, a regression or isolation test, a demo patch, an attached reproducer, or the report text itself ('the code is almost entirely generated by AI harness', 'the attached test patch, written by Claude Code', 'I had Opus write the demo', 'I used an AI coding assistant while preparing this', 'drafted with Claude Code'). Includes drafts a human later edited, and code a committer says was AI-generated.

The AI produced a side artifact used during the work but not submitted as the change: a benchmark or measurement script, reproduction steps or details, a webpage or diagram used to think it through, a findings report, 'AI-assisted validations', or an AI's quoted opinion pasted in for reference ('here is what Chat-GPT had to say').

An AI is referred to but did nothing for this work: a proposal to use AI in the future, an LLM-generated workload that triggered the bug, a feature for AI clients, an AI policy debate, a URL tracking parameter, a joke or aside, or a comparison. Exclusive with the four work roles.
